policy.resident_core: Rust is the default for long-lived Ninja-owned contracts, orchestration and agent-facing tooling.
policy.external_tooling: Use mature external tools in their native implementation. Ninja owns bounded adapters, provenance and contracts instead of rewriting upstream systems.
policy.python_boundary: Python is a first-class Ninja Labs research language for statistics, econometrics, ML, experimental optimization and backtesting where its ecosystem materially improves correctness or research velocity.
policy.implementation_rule: Catalog breadth does not imply implementation priority. Implement a capability when a registered experiment requires it.

tools.role: Historical web corpus and index before recrawling live pages.
tools.notes: Prefer archived historical material when it satisfies the experiment and preserves point-in-time evidence.

tools.role: Self-hostable metasearch for source discovery.
tools.notes: Discovery output is not evidence until acquired and preserved through a reproducible path.

tools.role: Current-topic, community and narrative reconnaissance across public sources.
tools.notes: Use for reconnaissance/source discovery. Synthesized output is not directly a historical market feature.

tools.role: External-information discovery and acquisition hub where its connectors cover the required source.
tools.notes: Treat connector output as source material; preserve Ninja temporal/provenance semantics before scientific use.

tools.role: Structured historical and prospective global news/event source for event, entity and story discovery.
tools.notes: Strong candidate for a second timestamped information stream and later cross-source propagation work.

tools.role: Sentinel for prospective page/resource changes and first-seen history.
tools.notes: Useful after a validated workflow identifies pages/resources worth watching continuously.

tools.role: Historical Reddit acquisition.
tools.notes: Current leading candidate for the first E1 information corpus, subject to source-quality verification. Preserve event-level timestamps and provenance.

tools.role: Efficient HTTP acquisition with browser-like TLS/HTTP behavior where ordinary HTTP is insufficient.
tools.notes: Use before paying browser-process cost when possible.

tools.role: Agent-oriented crawling, extraction and structured web acquisition when plain HTTP is insufficient but a fully interactive browser session is not yet required.
tools.safety_boundary: Use only for public or otherwise authorized sources. Access challenges remain explicit outcomes and do not authorize bypassing authentication, CAPTCHA or anti-abuse controls.
tools.notes: Prefer the nixpkgs package when available. Keep raw acquisition separate from semantic extraction and preserve source/provenance metadata.

tools.role: Crawler frontier, sessions, concurrency and retries.
tools.notes: Benchmark against Scrapy on a real acquisition workload instead of running two crawler frameworks by default.

tools.role: Mature high-throughput crawling and extraction pipelines.
tools.notes: Candidate workhorse when its pipeline model is a better fit than Crawlee.

tools.role: Normal browser automation for JavaScript-heavy public pages.
tools.notes: Browser acquisition is escalation, not the default for every source.

tools.role: Primary control path for an existing Chromium-family browser and authorized authenticated sessions without introducing another planner or agent runtime.
tools.safety_boundary: Use a dedicated agent browser profile and only sessions the operator is authorized to control. Human verification checkpoints remain human/session handoffs.
tools.notes: Prefer deterministic Playwright-compatible execution first. Keep the relay loopback-only and preserve task/action receipts where practical.

tools.role: Semantic browser fallback for fragile or ambiguous DOM interactions using observe/act/extract style primitives.
tools.safety_boundary: Use only on public or otherwise authorized browser targets; semantic automation does not change the authorization boundary.
tools.notes: Do not run as a competing orchestrator. Promote only if measured success or maintenance cost beats deterministic Browser Control/Playwright for the target workload.

tools.role: Hardened Chromium-compatible acquisition path when ordinary browser automation is insufficient.
tools.notes: Specialized fallback; measure success, latency and maintenance burden by source.

tools.role: Independent Firefox-derived browser engine for acquisition diversity.
tools.notes: Maintain engine diversity without making an experimental browser the only acquisition path.

tools.role: Specialized Chromium challenger for difficult web acquisition.
tools.notes: Benchmark information gain, success rate, latency and maintenance burden before promotion to a default path.

tools.role: Authorized HTTP(S)/WebSocket protocol observation, replay and debugging for sources and applications the operator is permitted to inspect.
tools.safety_boundary: Do not use to bypass authentication, intercept third-party traffic without authorization, extract credentials, or defeat access controls.
tools.notes: Treat captured flows as sensitive evidence. Record scope, target identity, capture time and artifact hashes; sanitize secrets before durable storage.

tools.role: Generate candidate OpenAPI descriptions from authorized mitmproxy captures so repeated browser operations can be evaluated for promotion to structured adapters.
tools.safety_boundary: Only reconstruct interfaces from traffic the operator is authorized to observe; generated specifications are hypotheses until validated against documented or controlled behavior.
tools.notes: Use as a reverse-engineering aid for interoperability and automation, not as an authority on undocumented semantics.

tools.role: High-fidelity browser crawling and WARC/WACZ capture for replayable web evidence.
tools.safety_boundary: Preserve only material Ninja is authorized to acquire and retain; replay artifacts may contain sensitive page state and require explicit storage policy.
tools.notes: Use selectively for mutable/high-value evidence that may change or disappear; do not archive the entire web by default.

tools.role: Main-content extraction from articles and HTML pages before normalization into observations.
tools.notes: Preserve raw capture/hash independently from extracted text.

tools.role: Structured parsing of PDFs, tables and complex documents before observation normalization.
tools.notes: Use OCR only when a usable text layer is unavailable.

tools.role: Analytical query engine over Parquet Bronze/Silver/Gold research data.
tools.notes: Preferred analytical substrate before introducing a resident research database service.

tools.role: Dataset and artifact lineage tied to Git revisions.
tools.notes: Introduce concrete DVC metadata/remotes when the first canonical dataset actually exists.

tools.role: Bounded adaptive experiment design and Bayesian optimization inside Ninja-owned experiment contracts.
tools.notes: Introduce after the fixed E1 pipeline works. Ax may optimize train/validation trials but must not access the untouched final test during adaptive search.

tools.role: Strategy backtest/runtime compatibility check for artifacts promoted toward Master Trader.
tools.notes: Do not use strategy backtesting as a substitute for E1/E2/E3 information-value validation.

tools.role: Code/configuration version identity.
tools.notes: Experiment records must reference the exact code revision used.

tools.role: Build and test the resident Rust Ninja core/tooling.
tools.notes: Rust remains the default implementation language for resident Ninja-owned control/orchestration code.
